about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

cotton.fundamental: Fresh Texas Plains yield reports describe drought losses on dryland fields, in line with the desk's above-USDA abandonment call; nothing new on demand. For old-crop Mar/May the supply story stays supportive, but the dollar firming and Brazilian real weakness keep export competition tough.
events: Texas Plains drought cutting cotton yields, Floyd County still leads upland output (Farm Progress, RFD-TV)
Mar/May cotton spread update as Dec delivery period nears (Barchart)
Cotton firm Monday morning with equities rebounding (Barchart)

sugar.fundamental: Brazil drives this: the real sliding past 6 per dollar to a 19-month low on the post-election selloff makes dollar sugar more attractive for Brazilian mills to hedge and export, which caps rallies. Monday's bounce looks like short covering rather than a change in Brazil's supply picture; Europe's weaker beet crop is a minor offset.
events: Real weakens past 6/USD, 19-month low as Lula selloff extends (Bloomberg)
Raw sugar rebounds Monday after last week's slide (Barchart)
Tereos cuts outlook on poor French beet harvest (Investing.com)

coffee.fundamental: ICE certified arabica keeps rebuilding (about 269k bags, up roughly a sixth in a month), which eases the deliverable squeeze that underpinned the Dec/Mar inverse. A real at a 1.75-year low encourages Brazilian farmer selling while November export registrations run close to October's pace, so deliverability from Brazil looks ample near term.
events: Coffee falls as ICE inventories rise and the real hits a 1.75-year low (Barchart)
Brief Monday rebound as the real steadied (ADMIS)
Cecafé registrations 3.43m bags month-to-date to 23 Nov (Cecafé)

cocoa.fundamental: Recent reports point to Ivory Coast port arrivals picking up after rain-related transport delays, and talk of ample global supply is weighing on prices; rising ICE certified stocks support that. Offsets are El Niño risk to the mid-crop and EUDR-related premiums in Europe; no new Ghana COCOBOD news since the 2030 bean-export-ban plan.
events: Cocoa eases as supply concerns fade and arrivals improve (Barchart/Nasdaq)
EUDR preparations lift European cocoa premiums (Bloomberg)
El Niño risk flagged for West African output (ADMIS)
